applied.replacement: SSDI provides disability benefits to eligible insured workers.

applied.quote: The SSDI eligibility rules in [20 CFR 404.315](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-20/section-404.315) and [20 CFR 404.130](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-20/section-404.130) contain no resource limit, meaning personal savings, investment portfolios, and spousal wealth do not disqualify a worker who paid into the program.
applied.replacement: The SSDI eligibility rules in [20 CFR 404.315](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-20/section-404.315) and [20 CFR 404.130](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-20/section-404.130) contain no resource limit.
applied.why: SOURCE does not list personal savings, investment portfolios, or spousal wealth.

applied.quote: When an individual receives both benefits, the [Social Security Administration](https://www.ssa.gov/benefits/disability/) (SSA) applies the unearned income calculation rules in [20 CFR 416.1121](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-20/section-416.1121), offsetting the SSI payment dollar-for-dollar after standard exclusions against the monthly SSDI distribution.
applied.replacement: When an individual receives both benefits, the [Social Security Administration](https://www.ssa.gov/benefits/disability/) (SSA) treats Social Security and disability benefits as unearned income under [20 CFR 416.1121](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-20/section-416.1121).
applied.why: SOURCE does not state dollar-for-dollar offset or standard exclusions.

applied.quote: If an applicant receives countable income exceeding the statutory federal benefit rate, they are completely ineligible for monthly payments.
applied.replacement: If an applicant has too much income under 20 CFR 416.1100, they are not eligible for a benefit.

applied.replacement: Claimants whose countable resources exceed these regulatory limits are not eligible for benefits.

applied.why: SOURCE does not mention personal investments or monthly asset compliance.

applied.quote: For statutory blindness, applicants do not face the same substantial gainful activity evaluations applied to physical or psychological illnesses.
applied.why: SOURCE does not describe evaluation rules for statutory blindness.

applied.quote: Medical determinations for both programs follow the identical five-step sequential evaluation process conducted by state disability determination services.
applied.why: SOURCE does not mention a five-step evaluation process or state agencies.

applied.why: SOURCE does not mention adjudicators or these specific evaluation steps.

applied.why: SOURCE does not state that approval in one confirms qualification in the other.

applied.why: SOURCE does not state a standard unearned income exclusion.

applied.why: SOURCE does not state this program purpose or income guarantee.

applied.why: SOURCE does not mention Medicare or a 24-month entitlement requirement.

applied.quote: The SSDI eligibility rules in 20 CFR 404.315 and 20 CFR 404.130 contain no resource limit, meaning your savings, owned vehicles, and personal real estate do not disqualify you from receiving worker disability insurance.

applied.why: SOURCE does not state SSDI is viable if work credits are lacking.

applied.quote: Existing administrative guides published on this site, citing the agency's October 14, 2026 cost-of-living announcement, confirm that millions of Americans receive concurrent benefits across both systems.
